data.title: Alphaddition
data.solution:
alphabet = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"

n = int(input())
v = int(input())
total = 0

seen = set()

for i in range(n):
    letter = input().upper()

    k = alphabet.index(letter)
    value = v + k

    if value % 2 == 0:
        total += value
    else:
        total -= value

    seen.add(letter)

    if len(seen) == 26:
        if total >= 0:
            total = int(total / 2 + 0.5)
        else:
            total = int(total / 2 - 0.5)

        seen.clear()

print(total)
data.statement:
Find the [[total]] of [[n]] letters. 
[[total]]'s initial value is {{0}}.

Each letter has a value based on the variable [[v]]: 

{{A}} = [[v]]
{{B}} = [[v]] + {{1}}
...
{{Z}} = [[v]] + {{25}}

If a letter has an <<even>> value, <<add>> the value to [[total]].
If a letter has an <<odd>> value, <<subtract>> the value from [[total]].

Treat the letters in a case insensitive manner.

There is also a <<WILDCARD>> factor- every time all the letters of the alphabet have been encountered, divide the [[total]] by two. Round to the nearest integer. If the result is <<exactly>> halfway between two integers, round <<away>> from zero. 
The letters do <<not>> have to be in order.

Once a <<WILDCARD>> has been activated, only the letters that follow count towards the next wildcard.

Example:
A
B
Y
... (All other letters of the alphabet)
X
Z <- The <<WILDCARD>> activates
A <- No <<WILDCARD>> activates, but a new one <<begins>> to form

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Find the total of n letters.
total's initial value is 0.

Each letter has a value based on the variable v:

A = v
B = v + 1
...
Z = v + 25

If a letter has an even value, add the value to total.
If a letter has an odd value, subtract the value from total.

Treat the letters in a case insensitive manner.

There is also a WILDCARD factor- every time all the letters of the alphabet have been encountered, divide the total by two. Round to the nearest integer. If the result is exactly halfway between two integers, round away from zero.
The letters do not have to be in order.

Once a WILDCARD has been activated, only the letters that follow count towards the next wildcard.

Example:
A
B
Y
... (All other letters of the alphabet)
X
Z <- The WILDCARD activates
A <- No WILDCARD activates, but a new one begins to form
Input
Line 1: An integer n.
Line 2: An integer v.
Next n lines: A letter of the alphabet.
Output
Line 1: The value of total.
Constraints
0 < n ≤ 105
0 ≤ v ≤ 100
Example
Input
10
0
F
i
R
s
T
t
E
s
T
a
Output
-31
